key_insight: A mean-flow adjoint framework with homogenized lattice Boltzmann modeling enables practical sensitivity analysis for porous-cylinder flows across steady, unsteady, and turbulent regimes without relying on expensive transient checkpoint storage.
engineering_relevance: This provides a computationally tractable way to optimize drag and dissipation in porous-flow designs and to support large-scale fluid-dynamic control problems, including LES-based turbulent cases.
method: Model cylinders as local porous media using Brinkman penalization within HLBM.
Compute mean-flow adjoint sensitivities for drag and energy dissipation.
Use automatic differentiation to generate adjoint kernels with SGS turbulence models and compare against frozen turbulence assumptions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic study from steady laminar to unsteady flow and a proof-of-concept turbulent test at Re = 3900, including direct comparison of AD-generated LES adjoints with the frozen turbulence assumption.
watch_item: Mean-flow adjoint results in chaotic/turbulent regimes can still be sensitive to modeling assumptions, so the validity of frozen-turbulence or SGS adjoint approximations should be checked carefully for each flow case.
paper_title: Mean-Flow Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis of Unsteady Flow Around Porous Cylinders Using a Homogenized Lattice Boltzmann Method
